forms.maxFieldsPerGroupSource: Miller's Law — working memory 7±2, reduced to 5 for forms (Designing UX Forms, Ch.4)
forms.labelPlacementSource: Eye-tracking research shows above-field labels have fastest completion (Designing UX Forms, Ch.6; Matteo Penzo study)
forms.errorTimingSource: Inline validation on blur reduces errors by 22% (Luke Wroblewski research, referenced in Designing UX Forms Ch.9)
forms.requiredIndicatorSource: Asterisk is universally recognized; legend 'Required fields marked with *' removes ambiguity (Designing UX Forms Ch.7)
forms.fieldSpacingSource: Gestalt proximity — tighter within group signals relationship (Universal Principles of Design, Lidwell)
forms.inputHeightSource: Fitts's Law — minimum 44px touch target (Laws of UX); standard 40-48px balances density and usability (Practical UI)
forms.placeholderUsageSource: Placeholder text disappears on focus, causing memory load (Nielsen Norman Group research, 100 Things #14)
forms.progressIndicatorSource: Zeigarnik Effect — showing progress motivates completion (Laws of UX)
forms.submitButtonPlacementSource: Left-aligned follows natural reading flow, reduces eye movement (Don't Make Me Think, Ch.3)
forms.autoFocusSource: Reduces first-action latency; starts user in productive state (Effective UI, Ch.8)
forms.maxSinglePageFieldsSource: Beyond 7 visible fields, abandon rate increases 15-20% per additional field (Designing UX Forms, Ch.2)

fieldJustification.source: Caroline Jarrett, Enders: 'Every field you include must be justified — if you can't explain why it's there, remove it' (Designing UX Forms)

emptyStateRequired.source: Andrew MacDonald: 'Never present a blank slate — always provide guidance, examples, or templates so users know what success looks like' (Fixing Bad UX)
